answer.answer: A provisioned end-to-end transport circuit through the optical core, connecting client-facing hand-offs and serving as the underlay for an external service.
The circuit’s transport quality class, expressing its physical path-protection and restoration level, such as platinum, gold, or best-effort.
An internal physical optical carrier—a wavelength on fiber—on which one or more transport circuits are carried; it is not itself client-facing.
The physical client demarcation point or port where the circuit terminates and presents to the client’s equipment.
Path-failure resilience for the circuit, implemented by switching to a diverse transport path when the primary path suffers a fiber cut or bearer loss.
A provisioned end-to-end transport circuit through the optical core that carries a client service between client-facing hand-offs and is itself carried on optical bearers.
The circuit’s transport quality class, expressing its physical protection and restoration level, such as platinum, gold, or best-effort.
The transport-internal optical wavelength on a fiber that physically carries one or more circuits; it is not a client-facing service object.
The physical client demarcation point or port where the transport circuit presents to and meets the client equipment.
The circuit’s path-failure protection mechanism, which switches traffic to a diverse path following failures such as a fiber cut or bearer loss.
A provisioned end-to-end transport circuit through the optical core that carries a client service between client-facing hand-off points.
The circuit’s transport quality class, expressing its physical protection and restoration level, such as platinum, gold, or best-effort.
An internal physical optical carrier—a wavelength on fiber—on which one or more circuits are carried; it is not itself client-facing.
The physical demarcation point or port where the transport circuit presents to and connects with the client’s equipment.
Path-failure resilience for the circuit, implemented by switching traffic to a diverse transport path after events such as a fiber cut or bearer loss.

An end-to-end transport circuit provisioned across the provider's optical core that carries the client’s traffic; the client-facing service is delivered over a dedicated bearer (instances like CIR-7).
The transport-grade of the circuit, i.e., its protection and restoration characteristics (e.g., platinum, gold, best-effort).
The physical optical bearer (a specific wavelength) on which circuits ride; an internal transport object with no direct client-facing meaning.
The physical demarcation point where the circuit presents to the client equipment; the client-facing interface location.
The protection mechanism for the circuit—provisioning a defense against failures via a diverse or redundant path (e.g., 1+1).

An end-to-end provisioned optical transport circuit (a dedicated path) that carries client traffic across the provider's optical core; it is the underlay service on which the bearer (wavelength) rides.
The transport-grade denotes the circuit's protection/restoration level or service quality tier (e.g., platinum, gold, best-effort) as the physical/operational class of the circuit.
The physical optical bearer (a wavelength on a fiber) used to carry circuits; an internal transport object not directly exposed to the client.
A demarcation point where the circuit presents to the customer equipment; the client-facing handoff to the client's router or interface.
The protection aspect denotes mechanisms to preserve service by switching to an alternate, diverse path (e.g., 1+1 protection) in case of failure.

An end-to-end transport circuit provisioning that carries client traffic across the optical core; an underlay service that the client rides, with a client-facing demarcation at handoffs (e.g., CIR-7).
The transport-grade of the circuit—the service class describing its physical protection and restoration characteristics (platinum, gold, best-effort).
The physical optical bearer (a wavelength / lambda) on which circuits are carried; an internal resource with no client-facing meaning.
The physical demarcation point where the circuit presents to the customer equipment (the handoff port/interface).
Protection of the circuit against a failure on the transport path by switching to a diverse or backup path (e.g., 1+1).
A provisioned end-to-end transport circuit through the optical core, carrying a client service between its hand-off points and serving as that service’s transport underlay.

The circuit’s transport-quality class, expressing its physical protection and restoration level, with example classes such as platinum, gold, and best-effort. The model does not define the precise guarantees of each class.
An internal physical optical carrier—a wavelength (lambda) on fiber—on which one or more transport circuits are carried; it is not itself the client-facing service.
The physical demarcation point or port where the transport circuit presents to and connects with the client equipment.
Path-level resilience for the circuit: switching to a diverse transport path after a failure such as a fiber cut or bearer loss, for example using 1+1 path protection.
A provisioned end-to-end optical transport circuit that carries a client service between hand-off points across the optical core.
The circuit’s transport quality class, expressing its physical protection and restoration level, with examples such as platinum, gold, and best-effort.
A transport-internal optical wavelength on a fiber that physically carries one or more circuits; it is not the client-facing circuit or its committed rate.
The physical demarcation port where the transport circuit is presented to and connects with the client equipment.
Path-level resilience for the circuit: switching to a diverse transport path following a fiber cut, bearer loss, or similar underlay-path failure.

A provisioned end-to-end client transport circuit across the optical core, presented at client hand-offs and carried internally on optical bearers; it is the transport underlay consumed by an external service.

A circuit’s transport-quality class, indicating its physical path-protection and restoration level, such as platinum, gold, or best-effort. The model does not define the exact guarantees associated with those grade values.
An internal physical optical carrier—a wavelength (lambda) on fiber—on which one or more transport circuits are carried; it is not itself the client-facing circuit or service.
The physical demarcation point or port where the transport circuit is presented to and meets the client equipment.
Path-level resilience for the circuit: switching traffic to a diverse transport path when the primary path fails, for example because of a fiber cut or bearer loss.

A provisioned end-to-end transport circuit (a transport-circuit) that carries client traffic across the optical core from one demarcation to another, defined as the underlay service that may be carried on a bearer and supports attributes like rate, latency, protection, and grade.

The transport-grade classification of a circuit, indicating its physical protection and restoration characteristics (e.g., platinum, gold, best-effort); used to convey resilience and service-level expectations.
The physical optical bearer (a wavelength) on which circuits are carried; an internal transport object (not client-facing) that the circuit rides on, e.g., a specific lambda on a fiber.
The demarcation point where the circuit presents to the customer equipment; the boundary between the transport underlay and the client IP/service attachment.
The protection mechanism for the circuit against transport-path failure, typically implemented as a defense like 1+1 path protection by switching to a diverse path.
A transport circuit: the end-to-end provisioned optical path across the core that carries a client service; it is the underlay on which the IP service rides and is carried on a bearer.
The transport-grade: the quality/restoration class assigned to the circuit indicating its protection level and recovery characteristics (e.g., platinum, gold, best-effort).
The physical optical bearer (a wavelength on a fiber) used to carry circuits; an internal transport resource (synonyms: wavelength, lambda) with no client-facing meaning.
The demarcation point: the physical boundary where the circuit presents to the customer equipment and where the service attaches.
Path protection: mechanisms to protect the circuit against transport-path failures by switching to a diverse or redundant path (e.g., 1+1 protection).
Denotes an end-to-end transport circuit: a provisioned optical transport path that carries a client service across the network core, with the underlay transport that the IP service rides on.
Denotes the transport-grade or protection/restoration level assigned to a circuit (e.g., platinum, gold, best-effort), indicating its physical protection and restoration characteristics.
Denotes the physical optical bearer (a wavelength on a fiber) used to carry circuits; an internal transport resource not exposed to the client.
Denotes the demarcation point where the circuit presents to the customer equipment; the hand-off/attachment point at the client site.
Denotes the protection mechanism for the circuit against transport-path failure, typically by switching to a diverse backup path (e.g., 1+1 protection).
